site.description: Mechanical Engineering student portfolio focused on Robotics and Autonomous Systems.

hero.summary: I’m a Mechanical Engineering student deliberately growing into robotics: designing the hardware, sensing the world, and building the control systems that let machines move with purpose.

story.headingEmphasis: Autonomy is where I’m taking them.
story.lead: Mechanical engineering taught me to care about the details behind reliable motion: forces, materials, energy, design constraints, and how systems behave in the real world.
story.body: I’m now extending that foundation into Robotics and Autonomous Systems, where the machine itself is only one part of the work. Sensors have to be interpreted, decisions have to be made, and the physical system has to execute safely.

focus.lead: I’m developing these disciplines together, because a capable robot is never just code, mechanics, or electronics in isolation.

items.title: Robotic Mechanisms
items.summary: Designing chassis, joints, actuators, and end effectors that can be built, tested, and trusted.

items.title: Sensing & Perception
items.summary: Using cameras, range sensors, and signals to give physical machines a meaningful view of their environment.

items.title: Autonomous Mobility
items.summary: Exploring localisation, obstacle avoidance, mapping, and planning for mobile robots in actual spaces.

items.title: Control & Embedded Systems
items.summary: Connecting models, sensors, and actuators through feedback loops that create precise physical behaviour.

projects.lead: These projects are intentionally labelled as concept builds until the prototypes, source code, test media, and measured results are real. No invented performance claims.

items.title: Pathfinder Inspection Rover
items.summary: A compact mobile robot concept designed to navigate a mapped indoor route, identify obstacles, and support simple inspection tasks.
items.challenge: Build a small rover architecture that connects mobility, sensing, and a clear inspection task.
items.approach: Start with constraints, make the drive and sensing interfaces testable, then log failures and iterate.
items.outcome: Replace this with only measured results, test conditions, and evidence once the project is built.

items.title: KinetiGrip Smart Gripper
items.summary: An adaptive gripper that explores compliant mechanics, servo control, and safe object handling.
items.challenge: Explore a simple end effector that balances grip force, object variation, and manufacturability.
items.approach: Prototype one variable at a time: linkage geometry, actuation, then sensing or feedback.
items.outcome: Add the payload range, repeatability, failure modes, and videos after testing.

items.title: NavSight Vision Stack
items.summary: A focused computer-vision experiment for recognising navigation cues from a low-cost camera feed.
items.challenge: Turn a camera stream into a small, explainable navigation signal.
items.approach: Define a visual cue, collect representative conditions, then measure where the method succeeds and fails.
items.outcome: Replace with dataset notes, test footage, accuracy measures, and limitations.

items.title: RoverTwin Digital Prototype
items.summary: A simulation-first experiment for testing a rover’s behaviour under changing loads, terrain, and power constraints.
items.challenge: Make design trade-offs visible before committing to hardware.
items.approach: Model a small number of relevant assumptions and compare outcomes against future physical tests.
items.outcome: Publish parameters, assumptions, test plots, and lessons—not unverified claims.
